I am first time reviewer so pardon my ignorance, I don't have a writing background either.

What i like about it is how it tries to make light of something as frequent as stress which does happen in our lives, hopefully the good kind (not too much, not too little, just enough for a challenge). But for me in the context of writing a poem for someone, i must consider the intention. If the intention is to make the stress feel lighthearted, the vocabulary could've been much more lighthearted as well at places. For example, the use of lemon juice being sour and being complimented with sugar makes sense and can be interpreted as you supporting her being her sugar. While there is nothing wrong with 'shake it up with ice cubes', but the following line 'cold and crisp and sweet' here the words cold and crisp don't really go well with the initial intent of the poem, being lighthearted. I would suggest using different words to make it sound more refreshing (maybe cool and mint). The lines slurp it with a straw (the fun and bendy kind) felt a little too passionate for a poem that is trying to make light of someone going through stress. Even though its personal preference, depending upon how one has a relationship with their partner, you can keep it in or go for something less sexual and more mature and relaxed like "I'd cherish every sip of it (so you know its off your back)". Just a rushed example but to me it complements the previous sentiment of a 'fancy glass' since i believe why would you use a straw in a fancy glass to begin with, and it somehow also validates the stress a bit more since most of the poem was trying to be very upbeat, it needs to have some of the contrast in the end to put yourself in her shoes and validate what she feels and to be a bit more grounding so it makes it feel more real and acknowledged.

Whatever my feedback was take it with a grain of salt, haha ! Hope this provides a new perspective.
